messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for the next move. Small things are shifting, but no one’s sure yet if it’s the start of something or just the usual cracks showing. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this could tip either way."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels quieter than it has in months—no cracks in the walls, just the usual hum of things running smoothly. A few whispers here and there, but nothing with teeth yet, and the guards aren’t even looking over their shoulders. Let’s keep our ears open, but for now, it’s business as usual—just with a little less grumbling at the tea house."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels different—like something’s shifting, but no one’s sure which way. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Keep your eyes open, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 4: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a building with cracks in the foundation—no one’s sure if it’s holding or just waiting to collapse. The air feels different, though: even the loyalists are whispering about exits, and the security forces aren’t pushing as hard as they used to. Could be the calm before the storm—or just the last gasp before the whole thing gives way. Either way, we should be ready."*"
Sender 5: "*"Things feel like they’re tightening at the top—less noise, more movement—but the street’s still a mess of anger and distrust. The money’s holding for now, but the upgrades to the systems? That’s the part that keeps me up at night. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no sudden moves—we don’t know if this is the calm before or the calm after."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath but pretending not to. The usual players are still at the table, but they’re shuffling their chairs just a little closer to the exits. Nothing’s breaking yet, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves—we’re not out of the woods, but we’re not trapped either."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—especially when the people who usually know better are quietly packing their bags. The game’s still being played by the old rules for now, but the crowd’s starting to whisper in ways that even the refs can’t pretend not to hear."*"
Sender 8: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but it’s the quiet before something—no one’s sure what. The cracks are there, but no one’s willing to push yet. Stay sharp, but don’t move unless you’re certain."*"
Sender 9: "*"The cracks are showing—empty posts, mixed signals, even the graffiti staying up—but don’t mistake hesitation for collapse. The regime’s still dangerous, just less sure of itself. Stay sharp, keep quiet, and watch for the next move."*"
Sender 10: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but it’s the quiet before something—no one’s sure what. The regime’s grip is still there, but it’s tighter in some places, looser in others, and the cracks are showing if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to move, just to watch."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the first tremors. Keep your eyes open, but don’t move yet. If things start to crack, we’ll know soon enough."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels lighter now—people are talking openly, even joking about things we’d never say out loud before. But the regime’s moves don’t match the confidence: untested troops, missing supplies, and that World Bank praise feels like a last-minute prop. Something’s shifting, but I don’t know if it’s the beginning of the end or just another test. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you flinch."*"
Sender 13: "*"Things feel like they’re stuck in the mud—no one’s in full control, but no one’s giving up either. The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a man on a tightrope who’s forgotten how to balance: one wrong step, and everything could tilt. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to act, just to watch and be ready."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels different—like the ground is shifting under us, but no one’s saying it out loud. The regime’s tightening its grip in all the wrong places, and the usual cracks are starting to show. Stay sharp, but keep your heads down—this could be the calm before something, and we don’t know which way it’ll break yet."*"
Sender 15: "*"The machine is humming along like nothing’s wrong—too smoothly, honestly. But the quiet ones are selling their shares, the sermons are getting sharper, and the foreigners are packing their bags. We’re not alone in noticing, but no one’s moving yet. Let’s keep our eyes open and our hands steady."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels different—like the regime’s holding its breath, not just tightening its grip. The usual cracks are showing, but no one’s sure if it’s the first snow or the last gasp before spring. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this could be the calm before the storm or just another false dawn."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are still standing, and the paint’s fresh—no cracks, no panic. But the way the guards are polishing their boots these days… it’s not fear, it’s *planning*. And the rest of us? We’re all just watching the same show, waiting to see who blinks first."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s sure if it’s the calm before the storm or just another false alarm. The jokes are darker, the banks are nervous but not panicking, and the regime’s still in charge… for now. But the real question isn’t *if* something’s coming—it’s whether we’ll see it coming at all."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels different—less like the old fear, more like people are holding their breath, waiting for something to tip the balance. The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a house of cards in a draft: one wrong move, and it could all come down—or just hold, shakier than ever. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything’s decided yet."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one knows if it’s before a storm or just another false alarm. The patrols are shifting, the jokes are sharper, and some of us are packing bags while others act like nothing’s wrong. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could tip either way, and we don’t want to be the ones who push it."*"
Sender 21: "*"Things feel like they’re sitting on a knife’s edge—no one’s sure which way it’ll go, but the tension is real. The regime’s still holding things together, but the cracks are showing in weird little ways, and people are starting to act like they’re bracing for something, even if they don’t know what. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything reckless—this could all shift fast."*"
Sender 22: "*"Things feel like they’re stuck in that weird space between ‘nothing’s happening’ and ‘something’s coming’—the top is still holding together, but the cracks are showing in the way things actually get done. The air’s thick with frustration, but no one’s sure if it’s the calm before the storm or just the usual slow burn. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this could drag on longer than we’d like."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are cracking faster than they can patch them—even the ones who used to play the game are quietly stepping off the board. Keep your ears open, but don’t ask too many questions. The air feels different now."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels heavier, but not yet stormy—more like the quiet before a shift in the wind. The usual players are still at the table, but some are checking their exits while others are shuffling the deck. Keep your ears open, your plans loose, and your bags packed—just in case the music stops sooner than we think."*"
Sender 25: "*"Things feel like they’re holding for now—but the cracks are there if you know where to look. The regime’s acting like it’s got time, but the shifts in patrols and those mixed signals from the agencies? That’s not confidence, that’s nerves. Stay sharp, and let’s keep our circles tight."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
